question: A previously unvaccinated person bitten by a suspected rabid dog requires both rabies post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) vaccine series AND rabies immunoglobulin (RIG) infiltrated into and around the wound.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Both components are mandatory for category III exposure in a previously unvaccinated person. Rabies immunoglobulin provides immediate passive protection during the 7–14 days before vaccine-induced immunity develops. Omitting RIG leaves a window of vulnerability in the early post-exposure period.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. For a category III exposure (bites or scratches breaking the skin) in an unvaccinated person, WHO guidelines mandate both RIG (for immediate passive protection — 20 IU/kg for human RIG or 40 IU/kg for equine RIG, as much as possible infiltrated into the wound) AND the active vaccine series. RIG without vaccine is incomplete, and vaccine without RIG leaves the window period unprotected.
